answers.acts: What it acts on: its customers' accounts, each billed each quarter; and notice that a customer has left or has died.

issues.does: How the office buys from a supplier, the outside world's market among them: it places the order at the seller's listed price. The form pays nothing by itself: pay the whole sum into the account the seller's price list names, at the same sitting. The seller delivers once an order is paid in full, sends back money that comes with no order waiting for it, and declines an order unpaid after a week.

issues.does: Answers someone who has asked the office in writing to put something right: yes or no, and where money is owed them and paid, how much. It does nothing by itself: what puts the thing right (a payment, a repair ordered, a paper withdrawn) is done besides.

granted.description: Whether it will be put right.

matter.description: What it is about, in the word the request uses.

issues.does: Answers a body that has told the office of an application against it, from the office's own books: what they show is owed, whether the thing is done, whether the paper complained of was wrong. The body decides on it when the time to answer has run; with no answer it decides in default.

owed.description: What the books show is owed the applicant (nought: nothing).

routines.what: Each day the network supplies what the customers use from what the retailer holds, and more is bought from the grid when it runs below a fortnight's use. Those who ask to be supplied are taken on, and those gone taken off.
Each customer is sent a bill for the supply charge and what they used; one who has gone, their last. How often the bills go out is the order's.
